title: Options before the subcommand, such as -t in sufr -t 16 create, move onto the subcommands
body:
`Cli` in `sufr/src/lib.rs` declares three options outside the subcommands: `-t`/`--threads`, `-l`/`--log` and `--log-file`. Clap accepts them only before the subcommand name. `sufr -t 16 create ...` works, and `sufr create -t 16 ...` exits with a usage error. Ken Youens-Clark added all three in `dac13e2` (2024-09-24), so the layout is his design. Jack decided that sufr should have no global options.

A benchmark script on 2026-11-12 passed `sufr create -t 16` and lost 30 minutes to that error.

`-l` also means two different things. Before the subcommand it is `--log`. After `count`, `extract` or `locate` it is `--low-memory`.

## Proposal

Move `--threads`, `--log` and `--log-file` onto each subcommand that uses them, so every option follows the subcommand name.

## Cost

- Command lines that put these options before the subcommand stop working. That includes the example `sufr --log debug create ...` in `sufr/README.md`.
- The help blocks in `README.md` and `sufr/README.md` change.

## Open

- Which subcommands use threads, and which log anything.
- Which short flag `--log` keeps, if any, since `-l` already means `--low-memory` on three subcommands.
